There is something empowering about giving your players the option to choose the way they want to play the game. PVE mode detractors will say that it separates the player base and that the whole point of the game is the potential threat of PvP. While I agree with this, there is something that they are overlooking completely.

There are people out there who derive enjoyment from ruining the experiences of other players. It is this small portion of the player base that must not be encouraged or rewarded. A large portion of the more casual, less competitive players have voiced their frustrations about this and a toggleable PvE mode was implemented as a test.

Good on you, Embark, for doing this and listening to your players. Now the power of choice is given to the players and they can choose how they want to play. Now players that want a chiller experience can get what they want. Players that still want PvP can still have PvP.

I suspect that most of the PvE mode detractors are simply complaining that easy prey is no longer available.

I honestly believe separating PvE and PvP into different modes is a huge mistake, and I really hope you reconsider making this change permanent.

One of the things that made ARC Raiders special was the balance between trust, tension, and unpredictability. In my experience, most of my lobbies used to be relatively chill. I rarely shot at other players unless I had a good reason to, and there was always that underlying tension of not knowing whether an encounter would turn hostile. That uncertainty was a huge part of what made the game so unique.

Since this PvE/PvP split, my experience has changed dramatically. Now, it feels like five out of every six players are immediately shooting at me or actively looking for a fight. Why? Because many of the players who previously preferred peaceful encounters have moved to PvE.

This creates a serious problem: players can now farm resources, accumulate wealth, and progress in a much safer environment, potentially without even needing to bring proper weapons. They can then enter the standard PvP lobbies fully equipped, with plenty of resources and money, while facing an environment where almost everyone is ready to shoot on sight.

In other words, the players who helped make the original PvP experience more varied and unpredictable are being pulled out of it. The result is a much more aggressive environment, where peaceful interactions become increasingly rare and combat becomes the default response.

**This isn't simply about preferring PvE or PvP. It's about how separating the two fundamentally changes the ecosystem of the game.** The tension between potentially friendly players and hostile players was part of the core experience. You never knew what kind of encounter you were going to have, and that made every decision meaningful.

By allowing players to progress in a low-risk PvE environment and then bring that progress into standard PvP raids, you risk creating an imbalance between risk and reward while also removing a significant part of what made the original experience engaging.

Personally, I believe this change could seriously damage the game's economy, its risk-reward loop, and the social dynamics that made ARC Raiders stand out from other extraction shooters.

I understand the intention behind offering players more choice, and I appreciate that you're testing different approaches. But I strongly believe that making this separation permanent would do more harm than good.

Please consider the long-term consequences before committing to this direction. The beauty of ARC Raiders was that peaceful players, opportunistic players, and aggressive PvP players all shared the same world. That mix was what made encounters feel organic and unpredictable.

**Please don't remove that dynamic from the game.**

I played this game on launch, and I lost interest because the stress of PvP (even with ABMM) was not worth playing this game. I love this game, I love the vibes, I love the feel- But I do not like PvP. This is a subjective opinion, a lot of people love the anxiety PvP adds to the game (since you never know what other people are gonna do), I am not one of them. I play games to have fun and relax with friends. Including a mode for people will never be an issue as long as the player base is large enough to support both sides, which many o' game has done in the past. People saying it has to be one or the other are really only correct if this game truly loses it's playerbase.

Issues with PvE:
1. The PvE mode as is, is obviously not fully done. I think the main thing that feels "missing" is the need to be quiet or stealthy; In PvPvE lobbies, your gunshots not only cause ARC to come over- But other players. Making noise is a problem, choosing to not fight ARC is a choice not just because of the ARC- But because you'll draw attention to yourself. That entire choice is missing from PvE. People are loud, it feels like the map turns into all out warfare. And it ruins the "vibe" of the game and some of the good decision making.
- My on the spot solution would be to make ARC better at hearing things at a distance in the PvE modes, not only to add to the danger of encounters but the choice of "Do I really wanna shoot at this wasp that will probably fly overhead, or do I need the materials and am willing to risk a Vaporizer coming by?"
- I understand it could be not only complicated to have different ARC difficulties across two modes, but I think it's the only viable way to keep the fear of "noise" in the game in-tact. Also, the fact ARC shoot at downed players is already a thing in PvE- And should definitely stay there; If not get harsher.
2. Rats still exist, in a way. My friend and I spent multiple expensive explosives and ammo taking down a Bully on Pandola, only for a cluster of people to run over from the shadows and strip the thing of everything valuable before we had time to even heal up. Even worse, there were flying ARC choosing to ignore them and shoot at us- So our Bully was completely dismantled by the time we got to it. This is a problem. I believe there seriously needs to be a system in place that dictates if you *didn't* help take down boss enemies, there is a set timer on the corpse before you get to dig at it. Not that you can't ever get to it, just a timer that keeps you from taking the loot from people who poured resources into taking something down. If people help provide a certain percentage of damage to the bot in question- Then the timer isn't a thing and it's free reign. I think that hits a good in-between. The way it is now, you no longer can defend your loot like you could in PvP. If someone tried that stuff there, you could blow their brains out and move on. I can't do anything here.
3. This attaches on to the fact that "noise" is no longer a fear factor. Everyone in the PvE modes is moving at mach-3 to get to the buildings before anyone else can, it's no longer "fighting" over buildings, it's rushing them. It causes people to not engage with the game or it's mechanics (fighting, traversal, cooperation) and just sprint to hot spots and strip it clean before others can get there with zero fear or hesitation. It's just bum-rushing. 

My main "fix" to all of this is the most simple;

PvE lobbies have less people in them. I know this could cause server issues, but with some expanded slots in this field, just simply having less players to deal with ARC (less players to be nearby when you take one down, less players to help you, less players to rush loot before you) could fix all my issues I have with PvE in it's current state.

All of this said, I love the fact the devs are checking it out, I literally would not be playing this game without this PvE mode right now. I hope it stays in, even in it's current state. The game is better with, rather than without.

Fresh take on extraction shooter genre with great sci-fi themes. Balanced PvP and PvE elements depending on your play taste. The game will place you in lobbies tailored to your individual play style (ie more PvP interactions will migrate you towards players with similar data stats).
Small dev team means that there has been some slow periods for content; what does get released is very high quality and innovative.

review: It enables me to survive
lots of fun, great graphics, good updatyes
PVE mode is in the game now!

I’ve been in the game for a while, so I can give you a balanced perspective on both sides of the negative opinions.

First, let’s talk about the addictive nature of the game. It’s definitely a game that keeps you hooked.

Now, let’s get into the PvP and PVE aspects. I’ve been on both sides, and both sides are what you expect.

In PvP, you have to be cautious of camping players and getting shot in the back. But you don’t have to worry about fake friendly players. You know what you’re coming for, and so do they. It’s always fight on sight now.

In PVE, the “friendly lobbies” are exactly how you’d imagine them: people running around carelessly. You do run into rats, but from my experience, the ratio is about 1/10 raids. I’m completely fine with that. You don’t have to constantly watch your back while looting. At the end of the day, you can’t have it your way all the time.

Finally, let’s talk about cheating. There was a time when cheating was bad and extremely noticeable, especially in PvP. But PVE players don’t tend to cheat. I’ll say it has cooled down, but if they don’t get the ESP wall hacks taken care of, this game is dead to me. I’ve lost a lot of stuff to cheating players and have only gained a tiny fraction of what I have lost.
